sections.h2: Who sends, values and collects the bill in Lyon County
sections.html:
The Lyon County Sheriff collects, the county's valuation administrator (the PVA) sets values, and the County Clerk takes over when a bill goes stale after April 15. The Sheriff's office handles about seven million dollars a year under KRS 134.140 and 160.500, which cover state, county, school and district tax on real, tangible and intangible property.

Find the Sheriff at 500 West Dale Avenue, Suite 100, Eddyville. Its mailing box is PO Box 126, Eddyville, KY 42038. The PVA operates from 500 B West Dale Avenue and answers at 270-388-7271. For prior-year delinquent bills, the Sheriff directs taxpayers to the County Clerk at 270-388-2331.

Both the Sheriff and the PVA work on West Dale Avenue, so one visit can answer two questions. Call before you go: the Sheriff cannot accept money until bills arrive from the clerk around the end of September.

sections.h2: Lyon County housing and the lake
sections.html:
Water covers a sixth of the county. Lyon County totals 257 square miles, 43 of them water, with Lake Barkley on the Cumberland River along its south side. Eddyville is the seat, and neighboring Kuttawa sits nearby. Both towns were relocated to higher ground when Barkley Dam backed up the lake. Interstates 24 and 69 cross at Eddyville, and Land Between the Lakes National Recreation Area faces Kuttawa across the water.

The county had 9,123 residents in the 2025 estimate and 4,889 housing units. Owners occupy 80.4 percent of homes, and 26.6 percent of residents are 65 or older. The typical home value is $189,500, typical rent is $747 a month, and typical household income is $65,066. The 2020 census found 4,780 housing units, with 30.4 percent of them vacant. The market is small and mostly owner-held, and a seller here often prices against lake access as well as square footage.

Storms have left marks on the housing stock. An EF4 tornado tore through Eddyville and the county on December 10 and 11, 2021, damaging or destroying hundreds of homes and businesses, and an EF3 touched down near Eddyville on May 26, 2024. If your house was repaired or rebuilt, tell the PVA, because the January 1 value follows the property's condition.

Your payment counts if it is received or postmarked by the date shown. The Sheriff gets bills from the clerk late in September, so statements normally land in mailboxes during early October.

Lyon County payment schedule
Payment windowWhat you owe
October 1 through November 1Bill minus 2 percent
November 2 to year endStated amount
JanuaryAdd a 5 percent penalty
February 1 until April 15 closesAdd a 21 percent penalty
Past April 15Clerk holds the bill; further penalties may apply

No bill by October 10? The Sheriff will send a duplicate. The tax year is the calendar year, so the bill covers January through December of the year printed on it.

The office accepts checks, money orders and cards, with the card processor charging a fee, and the same options are online. Partial payments are refused, though a single payment can cover several bills. For owners who find the lump sum hard, the Sheriff suggests checking for exemptions and asking a lender about escrow.

sections.h2: Who pays when a Lyon County house sells?
sections.html:
Kentucky addresses the bill to the January 1 owner, even if the house has since changed hands. The Sheriff says a closing agent or attorney usually works out each side's share of the year. Some agents then pay the Sheriff directly, and in other deals one party receives a credit and pays later.

  • Prorated payments are refused. Someone must cover the full bill.
  • Mortgage companies do not automatically get the statement. Lenders can pull data from the PVA roll, yet the owner must make sure the lender actually has the bill.
  • If a bill arrives in your name after a sale, send it on to the new owner at your former address.

Get the closing agent to confirm in writing who pays the Sheriff and by when, and keep the receipt.

Confer with the PVA first, then lodge the appeal at the clerk's office. State rules give you until the end of the workday after the roll's public viewing period closes, and that period opens in early May and runs about two weeks.

A local panel then takes up the matter about a month after viewing ends. It wants facts: photographs, an appraisal, insurance policies, construction costs or listings. A written decision explains any change and describes the next step to the state tax appeals board.

Bring photographs of the house, any appraisal, repair invoices and your insurance policy to the conference, and ask the PVA how the current value was reached. A conference often settles a question without a hearing, but the filing deadline at the clerk's office still applies if it does not.

Call the PVA at 270-388-7271 each spring for the exact dates, since the window can be shifted and the change is advertised locally.

A senior, or an owner classed as totally disabled, who occupies the home can deduct $49,100 from the assessed value for the 2025 to 2026 assessment years.

The Sheriff sends people who struggle to pay toward these exemptions and refers questions about them to the PVA at 270-388-7271. File with the PVA, not the Sheriff or clerk. Disability claimants normally reapply annually, except those with a service-connected disability and people whom Social Security or the Kentucky Retirement Systems has ruled permanently and totally disabled.

sections.h2: Selling a Lyon County house with tax owed
sections.html:
Get the payoff in writing from the correct office and let the closing agent pay it out of your proceeds. This year's balance comes from the Sheriff, and earlier years come from the County Clerk.

Delinquent bills get advertised before any sale, and the county attorney sends notices, so early action avoids added fees. Interest builds at one percent monthly once the clerk takes the bill, with clerk and attorney commissions on top. Have the closing agent pay any recorded lien from the sale proceeds so the house passes to the buyer with a clean tax record.

Bring the deed and your latest bill to the Sheriff's or clerk's office when you ask for the payoff, and ask how long the figure stays good. A cash sale moves fast, so having that number ready before you accept an offer keeps the closing on schedule.

faqs.q: Where does Lyon County send its property tax payments?
faqs.a: Payments go to the Lyon County Sheriff at 500 West Dale Avenue, Suite 100, Eddyville, or by post to Box 126 in Eddyville (KY 42038). An online link on the Sheriff's tax page also works. Past April 15, pay the County Clerk.

faqs.q: How large is the Lyon County early-payment discount?
faqs.a: It is 2 percent, for money received or postmarked between October 1 and November 1. The stated amount applies through year end, and a 5 percent penalty begins in January.

faqs.q: Will the Lyon County Sheriff take a partial payment?
faqs.a: No. Partial payments are refused. A single payment may cover several bills, and the Sheriff suggests checking exemptions or lender escrow if the full amount is hard to meet.

faqs.q: If I sell my Lyon County home in June, who pays that year's tax?
faqs.a: The January 1 owner is billed, and the closing agent usually prorates each side's share at the table. The Sheriff needs the whole bill paid, so confirm in writing who sends the payment.

faqs.q: How much is the Lyon County homestead exemption?
faqs.a: The deduction is $49,100 for seniors and totally disabled owners living in their homes, set for the 2025 to 2026 assessment years. Apply through the PVA at 270-388-7271.
